transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I guess what brings me in is... I keep planning my days around not having to drive over high bridges. It's just getting to be a hassle. And if I absolutely can't find a way around one, I just white-knuckle it the whole way across. I figured I should probably talk to someone about it.
Is it just driving over high bridges that bothers you, or do you also avoid other high places?

No, it's really just the bridges. I can go up in a tall building or stand on a ladder just fine. It's... well, I know those big bridges over the bay are built fine and folks drive them every day without a problem. But when I get near one, my mind just acts like the car could go right over the side.
Do you ever have episodes of intense fear or discomfort when you're driving over a high bridge?

Yeah, I definitely do. As soon as I see the bridge coming up, my chest gets really tight. My hands start sweating on the steering wheel, and I just kind of lock my eyes straight ahead. It's like I just have to focus on making it to the other side, no matter what.
Is it the thought of driving on the bridge that scares you, or could it also be the idea of being on the bridge in a different situation, like walking or being a passenger?

I'm not really sure about walking, to be honest. I haven't ever had a reason to try and walk across one of those big ones. But... yeah, even if I'm just a passenger and someone else is driving, it's pretty much the same feeling. I still get all tense and just want to get to the other side as fast as possible.
Would you feel afraid if you were to walk across a high bridge?

Well, like I just mentioned, I'm really not sure. I've never actually tried walking across one. I imagine I'd probably still be pretty nervous, just knowing how I feel when I'm riding in a car, but I can't say for certain since I haven't ever had to do it.
Do you think you would feel afraid if you were to walk across a high bridge?

Uh, like I was just saying, I really couldn't tell you for a fact. I've never actually walked across one of those big bridges. I mean, I assume I'd be scared, given how I get when I'm just riding in a car, but I can't give you a definite answer since I haven't ever tried it.
Is your fear of high bridges only present when you are driving, or would you feel afraid in other situations as well?

Well, like I've been saying, it's definitely not just when I'm behind the wheel. If I'm riding as a passenger in someone else's car, I get that exact same fear. As for any other situations besides that, I really just don't know, because I haven't been in them to find out.
Would your fear of high bridges be less if you were not in a vehicle at all?

Honestly, doc, I think we're kind of going in circles here. Like I've been trying to say, I just don't know. I've never been on one of those bridges outside of a car, so... I really couldn't tell you if the fear would be less, or if it would be worse. I just haven't ever experienced it to be able to give you a real answer on that.
Do you think your fear of high bridges is related to feeling like you're not in control?

I don't think so. I mean, I'm not really sure if it has anything to do with being in control or not. I just know that when I'm up that high on a bridge, looking down, I get scared. It's the height and the bridge itself, not really about who's driving or if I'm in control of the situation.
Is your fear of high bridges less about the bridge itself and more about the act of driving over it?

No, I... like I was just saying, it's definitely the bridge itself. The driving part doesn't really matter. I mean, I get just as scared if I'm just sitting in the passenger seat while someone else is at the wheel. So, yeah, it's being up high on that bridge that gets to me, not the act of driving.
Would you feel afraid if you were on a high bridge in a form of transportation other than a car, such as a bus or a train?
I really don't know. I've only ever gone over them in a car, so I can't say for sure how I'd feel on a bus or a train. I just haven't been in that situation to know.
Would you feel afraid if you were on a train going over a high bridge?
Like I said, I really couldn't tell you. I haven't ever been on a train going over a bridge like that. It's always just been in a car. So I don't know if it would be the same or not.
Would you feel afraid if you were on a bus going over a high bridge?

It's, uh... pretty much the exact same answer as the train, honestly. I've never taken a bus over one either. It's only ever been in a car. So I really couldn't tell you for sure how I'd react. I just don't know.
Would you feel afraid if you were in a very high place, like near the edge of a cliff?
No, I don't think so. Being up high like that doesn't really bother me. I've looked over the edge of a drop-off on a hike before and felt fine. It really just seems to be about the bridges for me.
Would your fear of high bridges change if you were to cross one on a mode of transportation that is not a car, such as a train or a bus?

Well, like I was saying just a minute ago... I really don't know. I've only ever crossed them in a car. So I couldn't tell you if being on a bus or a train would make it better or worse. I just haven't been in that situation to find out.
Would you feel afraid if you were to cross a high bridge on foot?

Well, it's... it's really the exact same answer again. I've never walked across a high bridge. I've only ever gone over them in my car, so... I just don't know how I'd feel doing it on foot. I really couldn't say for sure.
Would your fear of high bridges be present if you were on a boat going under a high bridge?

I honestly don't know. I haven't been on a boat going under one. But... if I had to guess, I really don't think that would bother me. My issue is being up on top of the bridge, driving across it. Just looking up at it from the water down below? I can't see that causing me any trouble. But, you know, I haven't actually done it, so I can't say for absolute certain.
Would you feel afraid if you were to be a pedestrian on a high bridge

Doc, I think you just asked me that a minute ago when you asked about crossing on foot. It's the same answer, really. I've never been a pedestrian on one, I've only ever driven across. So I just don't know how I'd handle it.
Would you feel afraid if you were on a high bridge in a vehicle where you have no control over the driving, such as a taxi?

I'm not really sure about that. I always drive myself, so I haven't been in a taxi or anything going over a high bridge. I don't know if not being the one behind the wheel would make it better or worse.
